transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We need to get the wrap disposition plan locked today so we're ready for Friday's dismantling. Per our standard wrap meeting protocol, I need each department lead to confirm the exact disposition and environmental-compliance requirements for your department. If anyone has an exception to the current draft plan — scenic pieces going to general salvage, selected hero props going to production storage — I need you to state the exact corrective requirement now so it can be entered into the meeting record before I can approve. Who wants to start?

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan. The antique jukebox listed as a hero prop is actually a rental, and its agreement requires it to be returned to the owner in its original condition. It cannot go to production storage or salvage. I confirmed this with the rental house yesterday but hadn't yet entered it in the wrap packet. The corrective requirement is: remove the antique jukebox from the hero props designated for production storage and instead schedule its return to the rental house owner in original condition before Friday's dismantling.

transcript.text: I have an exception to the draft plan regarding environmental compliance. The production's city green-film incentive requires at least 85 percent of dismantled set material by weight to be diverted from landfill. The approved vendor's audited plan reaches that threshold only through separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record. I confirmed the plan with the vendor this morning, but the compliance packet still contains the general-salvage draft. The corrective requirement is: replace the general-salvage vendor designation for scenic pieces with the approved recycling vendor's audited plan using separate wood and metal recycling bins plus a certified transfer record, and update the compliance packet accordingly before the plan is locked.
